sn35.18:1.2: But since there is gratification in sights, sentient beings are aroused by them.
sn35.18:1.3: If there were no drawback in sights, sentient beings wouldn’t grow disillusioned with them.
sn35.18:1.4: But since there is a drawback in sights, sentient beings do grow disillusioned with them.
sn35.18:1.5: If there were no escape from sights, sentient beings wouldn’t escape from them.
sn35.18:1.6: But since there is an escape from sights, sentient beings do escape from them.
sn35.18:1.7: If there were no gratification in sounds …
sn35.18:1.11: gratification in ideas, sentient beings wouldn’t be aroused by them.
sn35.18:1.12: But since there is gratification in ideas, sentient beings are aroused by them.
sn35.18:1.13: If there were no drawback in ideas, sentient beings wouldn’t grow disillusioned with them.
sn35.18:1.14: But since there is a drawback in ideas, sentient beings do grow disillusioned with them.
sn35.18:1.15: If there were no escape from ideas, sentient beings wouldn’t escape from them.
sn35.18:1.16: But since there is an escape from ideas, sentient beings do escape from them.
sn35.18:2.1: And besides, mendicants: so long as sentient beings have not truly understood, for what they are, the gratification, the drawback, and the escape of these six exterior sense fields, they have certainly not lived in this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—separated, wholly liberated, fully freed, with mind free of boundaries.
sn35.18:2.2: But when sentient beings have truly understood, for what they are, the gratification, the drawback, and the escape of these six exterior sense fields, then, mendicants, sentient beings have lived in this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—separated, wholly liberated, fully freed, with mind free of boundaries.”
